AS2Go · ATTACK COMPATIBILITY TECHNICAL REFERENCE
Technical reference · not a host scan
OS compatibility does not equal exploitability

An attack technique may be technically possible on an operating system while Credential Guard, account protection, the target protocol or domain hardening prevents individual prerequisites. This reference explicitly separates these layers.

01 · Scope and assumptions

This reference covers technical compatibility across Windows 10, Windows 11 and Windows Server 2019, 2022 and 2025. It distinguishes conceptual OS support from credential acquisition, authentication acceptance and tool-specific behavior.

LayerQuestionMeaning
OS compatibilityCan the system participate in the attack path in principle?Does not establish a specific vulnerability finding.
Credential AcquisitionCan the hash, ticket, certificate or plaintext actually be acquired?Credential Guard, LSA protection, account type and logon session are relevant.
Authentication AcceptanceDoes the target service accept the available authentication material?KDC encryption policy, ticket validity, permissions and certificate mapping must be assessed separately.
AD CS assumption: a suitable misconfiguration exists. WDigest assumption: UseLogonCredential = 1 is configured. These assumptions do not replace evidence of successful authentication or actual cached plaintext credentials.

Server columns primarily refer to the executing or compromised host. Statements about the KDC or CA explicitly identify that role. A Windows Server 2025 member server does not turn an older domain into a Windows Server 2025 KDC.

This matrix is a conceptual reference, not a laboratory test of every build or proof of compatibility with a specific tool. Windows 11 ≥22H2 includes multiple releases whose defaults must not be treated as identical.

A blanket “Limited” rating for OPtH/PtT conflates credential extraction with the use of existing material. Credential Guard isolates NTLM secrets and TGT-related secrets; its protection has documented limits. OPtH additionally requires a KDC that accepts the relevant RC4 request. [CG] [LIMIT]

Default, configured and actually running are three distinct states. A version string is not a substitute for telemetry.

04 · Overpass-the-Hash (OPtH)

What is being assessed

Overpass-the-Hash is a form of Pass-the-Key: the account’s NT hash is used as its Kerberos RC4 key to request Kerberos tickets, without knowing the plaintext password. Unlike classic Pass-the-Hash, the authentication path is Kerberos, not NTLM. The KDC must permit the relevant RC4 use. Using an AES key is the broader Pass-the-Key technique.

Role of Credential Guard

Credential Guard restricts acquisition of protected logon secrets from a compromised host. This does not establish that an independently obtained hash cannot be used to request a ticket. Evaluate credential acquisition, KDC acceptance and subsequent service access separately. [CG] [LIMIT]

Why the previous CIFS/LDAP footnote is removed

“CIFS works, LDAP fails” is not a general OS rule without a defined test setup. Record the service, authentication mechanism, account, permissions and failure cause separately. An LDAP failure does not prove an OPtH restriction or establish that PtT will succeed.

Assessment interpretation

  • Document the source host, KDC, target service and account.
  • Verify whether the KDC accepts the relevant RC4 request; NTLM acceptance is not the OPtH prerequisite.
  • Distinguish classic Pass-the-Hash (NTLM), Overpass-the-Hash (NT hash / Kerberos RC4) and Pass-the-Key with AES keys. Evaluate signing, channel binding and EPA according to their protocol-specific purpose.
  • Successful ticket issuance, successful service authentication and an authorized administrative action are separate findings.
Suggested report wording
Reference text
Technically possible when an account’s NT hash is available and the KDC permits its use as a Kerberos RC4 key. Credential Guard may restrict local secret acquisition. Ticket issuance and subsequent service access must be validated separately.

05 · Pass-the-Ticket (PtT)

Distinguish TGTs from service tickets

A Ticket Granting Ticket is used to request additional tickets. A service ticket is specific to a service. Credential Guard protects TGT-related secrets but does not provide identical protection for every ticket and credential store. “Credential Guard active = no PtT” is therefore too broad. [CG]

Assessment prerequisites

  • Record ticket type, service association, validity period and account.
  • Document the execution or logon session and the actual authentication path.
  • Assess ticket acquisition separately from subsequent access.
  • Analyze delegation as a separate attack path; not every delegation abuse scenario is simply ticket theft.

Credential Guard affects Kerberos unconstrained delegation. This is a specific protection mechanism, not a universal statement about all Kerberos or delegation scenarios. [LIMIT]

Suggested report wording
Reference text
The OS version does not categorically exclude the use of a suitable, valid Kerberos ticket. Whether such a ticket can be acquired depends on Credential Guard, session type and the specific credential store, among other factors.

06 · AD CS / Certificate Template Abuse

Keep terminology distinct

Certificate template abuse describes obtaining a certificate through misconfiguration or unauthorized issuance. Pass-the-Certificate describes its subsequent use for authentication. These steps are related but are not identical.

OS-level interpretation

The listed client and server versions are not blanket exclusion criteria based on version number alone. Enrollment context, CA/template configuration and the authentication path determine the assessment. This does not guarantee that a specific tool or ESC1 path works at every patch level.

Important update: strong certificate mapping

KB5014754 describes hardening of certificate-based authentication on Windows domain controllers. The February 2025 updates enabled Full Enforcement by default; after installation of the September 9, 2025 security updates, the previous registry rollback using StrongCertificateBindingEnforcement is no longer supported. Certificates that cannot be strongly mapped are rejected in enforcement mode. [CERT]

A template flagged as ESC1 warrants investigation; it does not automatically prove successful impersonation against a fully patched KDC. Evaluate the SID extension, strong mapping and actual authentication path together.

Record in the report

  • CA and template, including enrollment permissions and Subject/SAN configuration.
  • Issuance requirements and the certificate’s authentication purposes.
  • Patch level of the relevant DC/KDC and strong certificate mapping.
  • Certificate issuance success separately from authentication success.
  • The identity to which the certificate was actually mapped.

07 · WDigest: the registry value is not complete evidence

Matrix assumption

Registry configuration
HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\WDigest
UseLogonCredential = 1

This assumption describes a configuration prerequisite. It proves neither the presence of a password in an existing session nor the ability to read it.

Correction of the earlier blanket statement

“Registry configured = OK on every version” is too broad as a reliable attack conclusion. Credential Guard prevents using signed-in credentials for WDigest SSO. Applications may still prompt for explicit credentials; this is not equivalent to automatic caching of interactive logon credentials. [LIMIT] [CG]

Members of Protected Users do not cache plaintext credentials for Windows Digest even when Digest is enabled. Account protection must therefore be checked independently of the registry value. [PU]

CheckWhy it is required
Registry valueRead configuration; do not confuse it with an existing secret.
Credential Guard running?Affects WDigest SSO using signed-in credentials.
Protected Users?Prevents the relevant plaintext caching despite enabled Digest configuration.
Relevant logon / sessionConfiguration alone does not establish the actual contents of a session.
LSASS accessAssess protection mechanisms and permissions separately.
Suggested table label
Reference text
WDigest — Conditional: UseLogonCredential=1 assumed; Credential Guard, Protected Users and session conditions must be evaluated separately.

08 · Kerberoasting: a service ticket is not a TGT

Compatibility considerations

Kerberoasting targets service tickets. An SPN and the ability to request a ticket do not imply successful offline cracking. Encryption type, password quality and account type determine practical risk. [RC4]

Important clarification for Server 2025

Microsoft documents that Windows Server 2025 domain controllers do not issue RC4 TGTs. This must not be interpreted as a blanket statement that they never issue RC4 service tickets or automatically prevent Kerberoasting. The earlier phrase “no RC4 ticket grants” was imprecise. [RC4]

RC4 hardening and timeline

Updates starting November 8, 2022 changed certain Kerberos defaults toward AES-SHA1. Microsoft also describes phasing out RC4 as the assumed supported encryption type. For a specific environment, installed updates, account settings and observed ticket encryption types are decisive, not an announced roadmap alone. [RC4]

AES reduces offline cracking risk compared with RC4 but does not remove the underlying attack path. “AES in use” must not be reported as “Kerberoasting impossible”.

Recommended evidence

  • Document the SPN, associated account and its privileges.
  • Assess the actual service ticket encryption type rather than desired configuration alone.
  • Record the KDC role and patch level separately from the requesting host’s OS.
  • Assess service account password management and manageability.
  • Report ticket requests, offline attack feasibility and demonstrated compromise as separate results.

09 · Validation and evidence

This section documents what AS2Go checks, not the results of a particular run. Status prefixes, account names, domains, hosts, template names and observed outcomes are intentionally omitted. The coverage inventory is based on the supplied AS2Go output; exact detection rules must be verified against the collector implementation.

AS2Go check coverage

#CheckWhat AS2Go testsInterpretation boundary
1Local administrator privilegesChecks whether the current user has local administrator privileges.Separate account/group membership from the current process token.
2Process token elevationChecks whether the current PowerShell process is running with an elevated administrator token.A local administrator account can run a non-elevated process.
3LSASS PPL startup evidenceChecks for evidence that LSASS started as a protected process during the current boot.Missing evidence does not by itself establish that PPL is disabled.
4Credential Guard runtime stateChecks whether Credential Guard is running.Distinguish configured protection from actual runtime state.
5Virtualization-Based Security runtime stateChecks whether VBS is running.VBS and Credential Guard are related but separate observations.
6Defender real-time protectionChecks the Microsoft Defender Antivirus real-time protection state.A protection setting does not prove a specific technique is blocked.
7Defender behavior monitoringChecks the Microsoft Defender Antivirus behavior monitoring state.Keep this separate from real-time protection and the MDE sensor.
8Defender for Endpoint runtime indicationChecks whether Microsoft Defender for Endpoint is reported as running.Service state, onboarding and sensor health are separate dimensions; verify collector coverage.
9Kerberos ticket-cache identityChecks the client identity associated with currently cached Kerberos tickets.Cache identity alone does not prove ticket usability or privileged access.
10Remote administrative share accessChecks whether the current user can access the designated remote administrative share.Share access does not prove remote service creation or SYSTEM execution.
11WDigest credential-caching supportChecks whether WDigest credential caching is reported as supported on the current OS build.Keep build/tool support, registry configuration, account protection and session state separate.
12Risky AD CS certificate templatesChecks for risky certificate templates, including ESC1 candidates.A candidate finding is not proof of successful issuance, mapping or authentication.
13Overpass-the-Hash compatibility / readinessChecks the compatibility/readiness indication for the Overpass-the-Hash option.The original output used the legacy PtH label. Verify the check implements OPtH semantics before treating it as an OPtH result.
14Tier 0 accounts with SPNsChecks whether at least one account classified as Tier 0 has an SPN.An SPN finding is not proof of password recovery or compromise.

The inventory describes check scope only. It is neither a host assessment result nor a guarantee that every prerequisite is checked. OS/role queries below provide context; the examples are supplementary validation commands, not a reproduction of the AS2Go implementation.

Read-only validation examples

The following examples read existing state. They do not enable attack techniques or change security policies. Run within the authorized scope. Execution and coverage depend on permissions and host role. Record failures as Unknown or Not checked rather than automatically as disabled or secure.

Host identity, role and current token
PowerShell
Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_OperatingSystem |
    Select-Object Caption, Version, BuildNumber, LastBootUpTime
Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_ComputerSystem |
    Select-Object Name, Domain, DomainRole

$identity = [Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity]::GetCurrent()
$principal = [Security.Principal.WindowsPrincipal]::new($identity)
[pscustomobject]@{
    Identity = $identity.Name
    ElevatedAdministratorToken = $principal.IsInRole(
        [Security.Principal.WindowsBuiltInRole]::Administrator
    )
}
# This token check is not a separate inventory of local group membership.
VBS and Credential Guard runtime evidence
PowerShell
try {
    Get-CimInstance -Namespace root\Microsoft\Windows\DeviceGuard `
        -ClassName Win32_DeviceGuard -ErrorAction Stop |
        Select-Object VirtualizationBasedSecurityStatus,
            SecurityServicesConfigured, SecurityServicesRunning
} catch {
    Write-Warning "Device Guard state: Unknown. $($_.Exception.Message)"
}

Keep the raw arrays as evidence and interpret them against Microsoft’s documentation. VBS running does not by itself prove Credential Guard running. [DEFAULT]

LSASS protected-process startup evidence for the current boot
PowerShell
try {
    $boot = (Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem -ErrorAction Stop).LastBootUpTime
    $systemLog = Get-WinEvent -ListLog System -ErrorAction Stop
    if (-not $systemLog.IsEnabled) {
        throw 'The System log is disabled.'
    }
    # A successful query with no matching event is still not proof PPL is off.
    Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{
        LogName = 'System'
        ProviderName = 'Microsoft-Windows-Wininit'
        Id = 12
        StartTime = $boot
    } -ErrorAction Stop | Select-Object TimeCreated, Id, Message
} catch {
    Write-Warning "PPL startup evidence not established. $($_.Exception.Message)"
}

WinInit event 12 is documented evidence that LSASS started protected. Missing or unavailable evidence must not automatically become PPL=False. [PPL]

Defender Antivirus and MDE sensor observations
PowerShell
try {
    Get-MpComputerStatus -ErrorAction Stop |
        Select-Object AMRunningMode, AMServiceEnabled, AntivirusEnabled,
            RealTimeProtectionEnabled, BehaviorMonitorEnabled, IsTamperProtected
} catch {
    Write-Warning "Defender AV state: Unknown. $($_.Exception.Message)"
}

try {
    Get-Service -Name Sense -ErrorAction Stop |
        Select-Object Name, Status, StartType
} catch {
    Write-Warning "Sense service state not established. $($_.Exception.Message)"
}
# Sense service state alone does not validate cloud onboarding or sensor health.

[AV] [BEHAVIOR] [MDE]

Read WDigest configuration
PowerShell
$path = 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\WDigest'

try {
$value = Get-ItemPropertyValue -Path $path `
-Name UseLogonCredential -ErrorAction Stop
    [pscustomobject]@{
        Setting = 'UseLogonCredential'
        Value   = $value
        Note    = 'Configuration only; not evidence of cached plaintext.'
}
}
catch {
Write-Warning ('Value could not be read: {0}' -f $_.Exception.Message)
}

A missing value, a missing key and an access error are different states. Preserve those distinctions. The registry value is not evidence of cached plaintext.

Coverage of a prerequisite check must be distinguished from evidence that an attack technique was successfully executed.

AreaReliable evidenceInsufficient evidence
OPtHAvailable NT hash, KDC RC4 acceptance and observed ticket issuanceOS version or SMB reachability alone
PtTValid matching ticket and the session actually usedTicket cache presence alone
AD CSIssuance and mapping/authentication resultsA risky template name alone
WDigestRegistry, account/session protection and actual credential stateUseLogonCredential=1 alone

10 · Recommendations for AS2Go and assessment reports

Compatibility

Track OS compatibility as a separate property. “OK” means only that the technique is not categorically excluded by the version classification.

Prerequisites

Record known / missing / unknown for each prerequisite. Mark assumptions explicitly, such as “Template abuse assumed” or “UseLogonCredential=1 assumed”.

Outcome

Distinguish not tested, blocked, authentication succeeded and objective achieved. Do not infer any of these outcomes from a static matrix alone.

Recommended data fields

Reference text
Technique | SourceOS | TargetRole | CredentialSource
Prerequisites | CredentialGuardRunning | AccountProtection
TargetAuthentication | PatchEvidence | ValidationState | Notes

Prioritizing safeguards

  • Restrict privileged logons to trusted systems and separate administrative tiers.
  • Validate Credential Guard and other credential protection mechanisms for the supported role and workload. [DEFAULT] [LIMIT]
  • Consider Remote Credential Guard for suitable RDP scenarios; distinguish its protection model from ordinary credential forwarding. [RCG]
  • Assess AD CS misconfigurations together with strong certificate mapping. [CERT]
  • Remediate RC4 usage based on observed Kerberos activity and account configuration. [RC4]
